thread:
ben: RFC follow-up idea: what about a quorum-based fallback instead of purely local heuristics? controller publishes small per-region policy shards + a quorum threshold. Router/runtime consult local shard + peers (lightweight) to reach quorum before changing global routing. Pros/cons?

tara: Interesting. Quorum reduces noisy single-node decisions, but adds coordination latency. We could do a hybrid: runtime can short-circuit on critical failures (OOM/segfault) immediately, but otherwise require quorum across k=3 local routers in region before wide fallback.

yusuf: Implementation sketch: controller -> push policy shard to routers in region (seed, pct, min_confidence, shard_id). Routers gossip small heartbeat+health (1 byte) to k neighbors. If >=q of neighbors report low health OR local err_rate > threshold -> mark region-degraded and route to fallback. Keep gossip async and lossy.

ben: Good. Key constraints: make gossip tiny (bitset per policy shard) and TTL short (5s). Quorum defaults: q=2 of 3. Also provide an escape-hatch: if controller explicitly sets force_divert=true, routers must obey immediately.

tara: Telemetry: emit one-line event when quorum flips: ts node policy_v action quorum_count reason. Example: "2026-03-25T08:12Z node-3 p17 DECISION_FALLBACK quorum=2/3 ERR_RATE". Sample request ids at 0.2%. Keep payloads small.

yusuf: Edge: partitions causing split-brain quorums. Mitigate by preferring controller push when available; quorum only helps within connected region. If controller unreachable and no quorum, fall back to deterministic hash(seed||req_id) as safe default.

ops-bot: rollout-controller: shard v2 applied to region eu-west-1 at 2026-03-25T08:15:00Z
\b en: Operational knobs: shard_ttl, gossip_interval, quorum_k, quorum_q, force_divert flag. Default shard_ttl=30s, gossip=2s, k=3,q=2. Documented in RFC appendix.

tara: API: PATCH /v1/rollouts/:id/shards -> {shard_id, seed, pct, min_confidence, ttl, force_divert}. Router local debug endpoint: GET /local/quorum?policy=ID returns recent peer health bits + local decision (ops-only).

yusuf: Hedging still optional. If quorum indicates slight degradation, routers can hedge a tiny percentage (e.g., 1%) to fallback to gather confirmation signals without full switch. Hedge budget small.

ben: Action items: tara draft gossip bitset proto + example, yusuf prototype tiny gossip lib and perf note, I'll add quorum diagrams and runbook notes. We'll fold into RFC and pilot in simulate mode. /cc @tara @yusuf
